England and New Zealand collide in a crunch Nations Championship clash as the All Blacks look to respond to a shock defeat to Wales.
Dave Rennie's tourists were beaten in Cardiff for the first time in 73 years, but bring back a host of stars for this visit to Twickenham as they seek a response. The head coach admitted that he and his squad had "let the country down" in that Wales performance, heightening the pressure as they take on an England side relatively untested this November.
The hosts have swept aside Australia and Japan in impressive fashion across the last two weeks, but know the intensity will ratchet up significantly with the All Blacks in town. Having beaten their opponents this time last year, England are seeking to conquer New Zealand in consecutive games for just the second time in history - and the last side to do that went on to win the World Cup...
Follow all of the latest from the crunch clash with our live blog below:
England 5-0 New Zealand, 18 minutes
Jamie George delivers another fine lineout as England drive forward again having kicked inside New Zealand's 10 metres.
A knock out from England eases the pressure and hands them back to ball.
England ramping up the pressure
Here's more from Luke Baker at Allianz Stadium for us this afternoon
England 5-0 New Zealand, 15 minutes
Will Joseph flies forward with the ball and looks to spur England on.
They're not going far enough, quickly enough so kick for position and follow up with a determined press. A poor clearance kick from Roigard hands a lineout to England.
Then sweep the ball quickly to Cadan Murley who nips into a gap and raises the hopes of the watching crowd.
A kick to the corner looks to feed in Joseph but New Zealand get there first.
England 5-0 New Zealand, 13 minutes
New Zealand kick and a knock on from England hands the All Blacks the ball inside the English half.
Cam Roigard looks to feed the scrum but it collapses and England are given a warning.
Roigard delivers the ball, and Wallace Sititi picks it up. England's defence has work to do here.
Joe Heyes is penalised for clinging onto a knee whilst on the floor. New Zeland kick of position but then fling the lineout, and possession, over to England.
Lewis Moody joins England to stare down All Blacks haka
The former England captain Lewis Moody joined Maro Itoje and his squad to stare down New Zealand's haka in a spine-tingling pre-match display at Twickenham.
Moody unveiled his latest charity challenge this week to raise money and awareness having been diagnosed with motor neurone disease last year..
The England squad are wearing personalised boots in support of the former flanker against the All Blacks, and were joined by the 2003 World Cup winner as their visitors laid down their traditional pre-match Maori challenge.
England 5-0 New Zealand, 10 minutes
Great work from New Zealand!
England aren't given the time to develop an attack inside the 10 metres before the visitors reclaim the ball.
The All Blacks are growing into the game after a slow start.
England 5-0 New Zealand, 8 minutes
A great start from England who recover possession inside New Zealand's half.
They spread the ball to the right wing but are held at bay and decide to switch to the opposite side where Ollie Chessum probes the All Black defence.
The ball is turned over but the visitors don't hold onto it for long.
George Furbank takes a kick and nails a perfect 50-22. Advantage England again!
Perfect start for England
Luke Baker is at Allianz Stadium for us this afternoon
TRY! England 5-0 New Zealand, (Henry Slade, 5 minutes)
A penalty from New Zealand hands England the chance to gain ground.
Itoje claims the resultant lineout and England stride forward again.
Swift passing and a dainty kick from Fin Smith sends Henry Slade into the try zone and England take the lead!
The conversion is missed though.
England 0-0 New Zealand, 2 minutes
The All Blacks threaten to get inside England's 10 metre line but a knock on from Jordie Barrett hands possession to the hosts.
England set the scrum and the ball is fed by Jack van Poortvliet.
He collects and feeds Will Joseph who drives at the New Zealand line.

England thrashed New Zealand by a record margin in a remarkable performance at Twickenham to establish themselves as World Cup contenders.
The hosts ran rampant on their way to a 37-12 victory, beating the All Blacks in back-to-back meetings for just the second time in their history. New Zealand had promised a response following a shock defeat to Wales but were not allowed to find their flow, with England on top in just about every facet in a complete team performance.
Maro Itoje's men had been inspired by the presence of Lewis Moody, a 2003 World Cup winner, who joined the squad to stare down the haka ahead of kick off. The English players wore personalised boots in support of the former captain's battle against motor neurone disease, and produced a performance of which Moody could be most proud.
Follow all of the latest from the crunch clash with our live blog below:
The Lewis Moody message that inspired England to record win over New Zealand
England captain Maro Itoje revealed an inspirational speech from predecessor Lewis Moody inspired his side to a record win over New Zealand at Twickenham.
Moody, a 2003 World Cup winner who was diagnosed with motor neurone disease last year, joined Itoje and his side to stare down the All Blacks' haka in an emotional pre-match answer to the traditional Maori challenge.
The 48-year-old had presented Steve Borthwick's squad with their match shirts on Friday evening and addressed the side, setting the tone for a 37-12 success - their largest over the All Blacks.
How brilliant Ben Earl transformed himself into England's most important player
The final score of 37-12 and England's unfathomable 25-point margin of victory over New Zealand - the biggest All Blacks defeat to a northern hemisphere side in their history - were the stats that really caught the eye. But at the same time, Ben Earl was doing something pretty special himself.
Read Luke Baker's full piece from Allianz Stadium:
Maro Itoje reflects on impressive win
Here's England skipper Maro Itoje on the triumph
'Nothing has changed from the Six Nations'
England went just one from five for the first time in Six Nations history earlier this year, whereas they're now flying with five wins from six in the group stage of the Nations Championship.
But Ellis Genge is adamant that nothing fundamental has changed in that time
Nations Championship schedule, results and finals weekend permutations
What a result for England. Have a look at how that impacts the standings in the Nations Championship and the permutations for who will face on on Finals Weekend
REPORT: England summon spirit of World Cup winners in remarkable All Blacks thrashing
The last England side to conquer the All Blacks in back-to-back meetings went on to rule the world and on the evidence of this fantastical, fanciful afternoon, Steve Borthwick's men may yet have hope of emulating them.
Twickenham has known a few remarkable rugby days but seldom anything quite like this; not even in 2012, when England ran riot, has this mighty New Zealand team been reduced to rubble quite so spectacularly.
It was an English performance of the heady halcyon days, summoning the spirit of 2003 with a World Cup winner setting the tone.
Perhaps we should have known what was to come when Lewis Moody strode out to join Maro Itoje's men to stare down the haka - the former captain wore white again in a show of unity as he faces a battle beyond rugby; it proved a spell-binding start to a quite extraordinary afternoon.
Read Harry Latham-Coyle's full report from Allianz Stadium
Turmoil for New Zealand?
Two losses in a row for New Zealand after their shock defeat to Wales last week. It's not often the All Blacks suffer back-to-back defeats.
Plenty for Dave Rennie to ponder, especially with a potential rematch against England here, depending on how the tables end up
FULL-TIME! England 37-12 New Zealand
The biggest win by a northern hemisphere side over New Zealand. Wow! It was complete and utter domination
FULL-TIME! England 37-12 New Zealand
Simple three points for Marcus Smith to finish things off here. The full-time whistle blows! What a performance by England.
They were mesmerising, brilliant. The best performance of Steve Borthwick's reign and the crowd roar their approval.
The great All Blacks were outclassed in every facet. It was amazing from the hosts.
England 34-12 New Zealand, 79 mins
England burst into the 22 and offloads keep it alive before a long pass to George Furbank lurking on the right wing gets them close.
Back for the penalty about 15 metres out, in the centre of the pitch. England will take the three points - that should see out the remaining time.
